intro: Today's briefing covers Armenia's constitutional reform debate, ANCA's challenge to the Library of Congress, expanding Armenia-UAE ties, the TRIPP railway project, economic growth figures, and regional energy and trade developments.

topics.title: Armenia's draft constitution sparks debate on governance and media independence
topics.text: Armenian Weekly details what is changing in the proposed constitution and why it matters, while CivilNet raises concerns about media funding transparency and independence. Former President Ter-Petrosyan described recent statements by journalists and judges as turning points that Prime Minister Pashinyan cannot escape.

topics.title: ANCA challenges Library of Congress over Azerbaijani claims to Yerevan
topics.text: The Armenian National Committee of America is contesting the Library of Congress over Azerbaijani assertions regarding Armenia's capital. The challenge was reported by Asbarez, Armenian Weekly, and Oragark, indicating coordinated advocacy across diaspora outlets.

topics.title: Armenia and UAE deepen cooperation with frequent flights and planned agreements
topics.text: Around 30 direct flights operate weekly between Armenia and the UAE, and the two governments plan to sign a memorandum on exchanging experience in early 2027. An official reception in Yerevan marked the UAE's 55th founding anniversary, and the economy minister highlighted the UAE's potential role in regional economic ties.

topics.title: U.S. warns Russian management of Armenian railways will impact TRIPP project
topics.text: Asbarez reports that the United States says Russian management of Armenia's railways will affect the TRIPP project. A former aide to President George W. Bush assessed the likelihood of TRIPP's implementation, and News.am covered the same assessment in both its politics and society sections.

topics.title: Armenia's economic activity grows 6.4% in January-October 2026
topics.text: Armenpress reports that Armenia's economic activity increased by 6.4% in the first ten months of 2026, with foreign trade turnover up 1.2% over the same period. The Central Bank published exchange rates and precious metals prices, and the regulator adopted a framework for energy storage facilities.

topics.title: Armenia could join European power grid via Turkey; civil society award for Eurovote initiative
topics.text: CivilNet reports Armenia could connect to the European power grid through Turkey. Meanwhile, Armenia's Eurovote initiative won the 2026 Eastern Partnership Civil Society Award, as noted by ArmRadio.

topics.title: Kremlin confirms preparation for Pashinyan's visit to Russia
topics.text: Kremlin spokesman Peskov said preparations are underway for Prime Minister Pashinyan's visit to Russia, to be announced additionally. News.am also reported the Kremlin's statement on the upcoming visit.
